summary: Reference for every input pin on the Main Material Node (Base Color, Metallic, Specular, Roughness, Anisotropy/Tangent, Emissive, Opacity, Opacity Mask, Normal, WPO, Subsurface, Custom Data, AO, Refraction, Pixel Depth Offset, Shading Model) and which Blend Mode, Shading Model or Material Domain enables each.
gotchas: Disabled (grey) inputs mean Blend Mode/Shading Model/Domain is wrong, e.g. Opacity needs Translucent
WPO beyond original bounds causes culling/shadow errors; Scale Bounds compensates at a cost
Ambient Occlusion input is ignored with Movable lights (needs Static/Stationary baked lighting)
Anisotropy only on supported Gen5 platforms at High/Epic/Cinematic scalability

summary: Explains Hardware Ray Tracing costs (BLAS rebuilds for skinned/dynamic meshes, per-frame TLAS build, ray traversal, hit shading) and the cvars, stats and debug views to measure and cut them, including culling, WPO handling, memory residency, Far Field and a 60 fps cvar list.
gotchas: High-poly Skeletal Meshes rebuild BLAS every frame and quickly become a major GPU cost
WPO ignored in ray tracing by default; opt-in only works ~50 m around camera
Heavy mesh overlap (kitbashing, skyboxes, grass) makes traversal very slow; disable Visible in Ray Tracing
Traversal debug visualization modes are console-only

summary: How to make a Light Function material (Material Domain = Light Function, output to Emissive) to mask/animate a light (clouds, caustics, stencils), its light properties, and the Light Function Atlas that bakes them into tiles for cheaper rendering with colored support.
keys: Single Layer Water Uses Light Function Atlas
gotchas: Only Movable or Stationary lights; cannot be baked into lightmaps
Atlas materials cannot sample depth buffer, world position or GBuffer, and UVs should not be manipulated
Directional Lights are currently forced not to sample the atlas
Colored light functions need Deferred Lighting Uses Light Function Atlas enabled

summary: Tutorial for building translucent materials (Blend Mode Translucent, Opacity parameter), adding reflections via Surface TranslucencyVolume, tinted glass with Thin Translucent, checking overdraw in Shader Complexity, and fixing draw-order with Translucency Sort Priority.
gotchas: Translucent colored shadows only work with Static Lighting and Lightmass
Many reflective translucent materials hurt performance
Overdraw from stacked translucency gets expensive per layer
Changing Translucency Sort Priority can cause new sorting issues for spawned effects; define a convention

summary: Covers Volumetric Fog on the Exponential Height Fog component: global settings, per-light Volumetric Scattering Intensity and Cast Volumetric Shadow, local fog via Volume-domain particle materials, temporal reprojection, baked lighting, performance and unsupported features.
gotchas: Shadow-casting Point/Spot lights cost about 3x in fog
Fast-moving lights (flashlights, muzzle flashes) leave trails from temporal reprojection; set their scattering to 0
Volume materials only work on particles
Not supported: IES/Light Functions on point/spot lights, Source Radius, fog center decoupled from camera

summary: Scalability and tuning guide for Lumen GI and reflections: quality levels via sg.GlobalIlluminationQuality/sg.ReflectionQuality, Lumen Lite (Irradiance Final Gather), Software vs Hardware Ray Tracing costs, reflection roughness/downsample cvars, radiance cache and screen probe gather controls, and profiling.
gotchas: Low scalability disables Lumen entirely
Moving Static-mobility actors invalidates the Global Distance Field static cache (expensive)
Hit Lighting for Reflections is too expensive for games unless materials are trivial
Disable Async Compute (r.Lumen.AsyncCompute 0) when profiling Lumen alone

summary: How to create HLOD Layer assets (Instancing, Merged Mesh, Simplified Mesh) for World Partition, assign actors to them, build HLODs via Build > Build HLODs or the WorldPartitionHLODsBuilder commandlet, and visualize them in editor and at runtime.
gotchas: Actors must have Mobility set to Static to get HLODs
HLODs are not rebuilt unless source actors, meshes, materials or textures changed
Cell Size and Loading Range unavailable when layer is Always Loaded

summary: Reference for the Blend_* material functions that combine a Base and Blend Vector3 like Photoshop layer blend modes (Color Burn/Dodge, Darken, Difference, Exclusion, Hard/Linear/Pin/Soft Light, Lighten, Linear Burn/Dodge, Overlay, Screen).

Reference for procedural gradient material functions built from UV channel 0 (radial, diamond, linear U/V) plus SmoothCurve and ValueStep for reshaping or thresholding a gradient, avoiding gradient textures.
Reference for color-correction material functions applied to textures in-shader: 3ColorBlend, CheapContrast/CheapContrast_RGB, SCurve, 3PointLevels, HueShift and SmoothThreshold, with their inputs.
gotchas: CheapContrast and 3PointLevels take scalars; use CheapContrast_RGB for full-color images
Inputs labelled with dashes on 3PointLevels are separators, not real inputs

summary: Reference for the Math material functions AddComponents, Pi, LinearSine (time-driven linear/rounded waves) and VectorToRadialValue (vector or UV to angle/radial coordinates).
gotchas: AddComponents: use the output matching the input width (f2/f3/f4)

summary: Reference for miscellaneous material functions: TimeWithSpeedVariable, OffsetAndScaleTo1, PassThrough, SplitComponents and Flipbook (play a sprite-sheet texture as an animation by rows/columns).
gotchas: Flipbook uses time automatically when Animation Phase is unconnected

summary: Documents the single Particles-category material function 3dParticleOpacity, which fades particles using a depth texture, near-camera falloff and particle alpha, and outputs Opacity plus a camera-offset World Position Offset.
gotchas: Disable sRGB on the depth texture
Falloff inputs expect reciprocal values (1/n)

summary: Reference for procedural texture material functions: GeneratedBand and GeneratedOffsetBands for UV bands, NormalFromHeightmap to derive a normal map from a heightmap TextureObject, and the animated NormalFromHeightmapChaos.
gotchas: NormalFromHeightmap takes a TextureObject, not a TextureSample
NormalFromHeightmapChaos is expensive and may lack a heightmap input (page gives steps to add one)

summary: Reference for reflection material functions that align a spherical reflection texture to the view or world (ViewAlignedReflection, WorldAlignedReflection) and build a custom reflection vector from a normal map.
gotchas: Reflection texture input must be spherical

summary: Reference for FuzzyShading (velvet/moss Fresnel-like look) and FuzzyShadingGrass (grass diffuse with desaturated, recolored edges) material functions and their inputs.

Reference for texturing material functions: world/local-aligned and triplanar projection (WorldAlignedTexture, WorldAlignedNormal, WorldCoordinate3Way), DetailTexturing, CylindricalUVs, TextureCropping, CustomRotator, HeightLerp, SubUV_Function sprite sheets, TwoSidedTexturing and more.
gotchas: World-space projected textures swim on moving/animated objects
LocalAlignedTexture Normal input is nonfunctional
CameraWorldBlend appears still in development and may not give expected results
TwoSidedTexturing does nothing unless the material is Two Sided

summary: Explains Material Functions as reusable graph assets: FunctionInput/FunctionOutput nodes and input types, Expose to Library, preview values, passing texture and static bool parameters, propagation of edits, nesting, compile errors and where default functions live.
gotchas: Deleting a function input/output breaks links in all using Materials and cannot be undone
Editing default engine functions changes them everywhere; duplicate first
No circular nesting of functions
New functions may need an editor restart to appear in the library

summary: Documents the VectorOps Fresnel material function, which lets you supply custom normal and camera vectors, invert, set power and optionally apply CheapContrast, unlike the built-in Fresnel expression.

Reference for vertex-animation WPO material functions: SimpleGrassWind for foliage sway, SplineThicken, CameraOffset for depth sorting, ObjectPivotPoint, ObjectScale, PivotAxis, RotateAboutWorldAxis_cheap, StaticMeshMorphTargets and Wind.
gotchas: SimpleGrassWind should be the last WPO node added
ObjectPivotPoint and ObjectScale only work in the vertex shader, not the pixel shader
SplineThicken meshes must be very thin, normalized UVs, imported with Remove Degenerate Triangles disabled
PivotAxis supports only uniform scaling

summary: How to set Shading Model to From Material Expression and drive the Shading Model pin with Shading Model nodes, blending per pixel via BlendMaterialAttributes, If expressions or Switch nodes so one material (one draw call) uses several shading models.
gotchas: A Material Instance cannot be overridden to From Material Expression unless the parent uses it (fails silently)
Used Shading Models list may not match what is actually compiled when Switch nodes remove branches
Unlit shading model is not properly supported in this path
Shading Model pin shows enabled with Material Attributes nodes even when it does nothing

summary: Describes the cheap Subsurface shading model (MLM_Subsurface) for wax, jade or ice: how Subsurface Color and Opacity control scattering density, normal influence and shadow softness, plus its limitations.
gotchas: Default Opacity 1 gives a weak effect; set around 0.1
Point light shadowing not supported
Cascaded Shadow Map seams and light leaking near shadow casters
Lower quality than skin-oriented subsurface techniques

summary: How to create a MaterialParameterCollection asset of global scalar/vector parameters, read it in materials with a CollectionParameter node, and change values at runtime from Blueprint with Set Scalar Parameter Value, plus its limits.
gotchas: A Material can reference at most two Material Parameter Collections
Max 1024 scalar and 1024 vector parameters per collection
Changing the parameter count recompiles every material that references the collection
Renaming a parameter breaks Blueprint references (materials keep working)

summary: Reference of every Mesh Distance Field setting: Project Settings (Generate Mesh Distance Fields, voxel density), light properties for distance field shadows, Sky Light DFAO occlusion controls, Static Mesh Editor build/general settings and per-actor distance field options.
gotchas: Generate Mesh Distance Fields raises build time and memory even if unused, and needs an editor restart
Changing Distance Field Voxel Density rebuilds all distance fields and needs restart; large values eat memory
Adjust Ray Start Offset Depth Scale only by small amounts
Affect Distance Field Lighting requires Cast Shadow enabled

summary: Short how-to: enable Distance Field Ambient Occlusion by adding a Sky Light set to Movable once Generate Mesh Distance Fields is on; points to the Sky Light DFAO settings reference.
gotchas: Requires Generate Mesh Distance Fields in Project Settings > Rendering

summary: How-to for Distance Field Indirect Shadows: enable Generate Mesh Distance Fields per Static Mesh, set the actor Movable, enable Distance Field Indirect Shadow and build lighting so movable meshes cast soft shadows in baked indirectly lit areas.
gotchas: Relies on precomputed lighting (Volumetric Lightmaps) from a lighting build
Shadows are nearly invisible in directly or brightly lit areas

summary: How-to for enabling Distance Field Shadows on Directional, Point or Spot lights (Movable/Stationary) to shadow beyond the Cascaded Shadow Map Dynamic Shadow Distance, with a tip for isolating DF shadows when debugging.
gotchas: Option is greyed out unless Generate Mesh Distance Fields is enabled and light is Movable or Stationary
For Directional Lights DF shadows only apply beyond the CSM Dynamic Shadow Distance

summary: Mobile Rendering Features Reference: tables of which post-process, lighting, light mobility, material, texture and Niagara features are supported on Mobile Forward, Mobile Deferred and HDR-disabled mobile XR paths (OpenGL ES 3.2, Android Vulkan, Metal 2.0).
gotchas: Mobile paths support no Nanite, Lumen, Virtual Shadow Maps, TSR or hardware ray tracing

summary: Workflows for mixing Nanite and non-Nanite use of the same assets: importing a high-res Nanite mesh over an existing LOD chain, the Nanite Pass Switch node, the Nanite Override Material slot, per-actor Disallow Nanite, Nanite landscapes, and typical Nanite GPU timings.
keys: Level of Detail > High Res > Import High Res
gotchas: Nanite Override Material is forced to None in material instances, so it is not inherited from the parent
Nanite landscape does not raise landscape resolution, only adds culling/streaming/LOD benefits
Very high instance counts and many unique materials increase Nanite cost

summary: How to create Chaos Destruction Geometry Collection assets in Fracture Mode from Static Meshes, Blueprints or other collections, fracture them with Uniform Voronoi, simulate, and set interior-surface materials, plus mesh best practices.
gotchas: Source meshes must be watertight (no open faces) or simulation is unpredictable
Source pieces must not intersect; the solver pushes overlapping pieces apart
With multiple selected actors, the first selected sets the pivot

summary: Lists hardware (SLAT CPU, BIOS virtualization, 4 GB RAM) and OS/Docker requirements for building and running Unreal Engine's Linux and Windows container images, with Docker install links.
gotchas: Beta feature
Windows container images build/run only on Windows 10 Pro/Enterprise/Education 1809+

summary: How to create and edit Landscape Splines in Landscape Mode (Manage > Spline) for roads, paths and fences: placing/joining/splitting control points, assigning spline meshes, applying them to the heightmap via a Spline edit layer, selection tools, and all control point and segment properties.
gotchas: Splines do not change the heightmap until a Spline edit layer is added to the edit layer stack
Select All affects every spline actor in the level; use Select Spline Points/Segments for one graph
Scale gizmo on splines edits tangents instead of scaling
